notes: Three university-layer documents (catalog academic-integrity policy, Office of AI syllabus guidance, IT-5-136 GenAI security policy). Main disagreements: (1) phase for rule sentences inside definitions and sample syllabus statements (general or course-start vs during-work); resolved to during-work when the sentence governs how students do their work, general for rationale and scope sentences. (2) actor for rationale, scope and contact sentences (admin vs all); resolved to all when no addressee is named. (3) Type: P68 vs P57 for the instructor-student discussion before a sanction (P57); P29 vs P32 for 'final submission must predominantly reflect the student's original thought' (P32); P50 vs P61 for the public-GenAI definition (P61); P01 vs P06 for the Example 1 default ban (P01). (4) Modality: nondisclosure as a violation (must-not) and 'will be considered academic misconduct' (informs). (5) Document stance: IT-5-136 was restrict (A) vs permit (B); resolved to permit because it limits data, not AI use. Units found by only one coder were all real policy sentences and were kept, except one heading and two exact or near-exact repeats of Example 3 sentences in Example 4, which were dropped. Coder B's single merged sanctions unit was split to match coder A's separate escalated-sanctions unit.
